Rashi on Ketubot 75b:1:1.english: He cannot claim - Because he knew [of them] and was reconciled [to them].

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:2:1.hebrew: הבעל מהימן - דאמר: הואיל וספק הוא אם הטעתו ואם לאו, העמד ממון על חזקתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:2:1.english: The husband is deemed credible - For he says: Since it is uncertain whether she deceived him or not, leave the money in its presumptive possession.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:2:2.hebrew: מני רבי יהושע היא דאמר - בפ"ק: היא אומרת משארסתני נאנסתי והוא אומר עד שלא ארסתיך — לא מפיה אנו חיין שתהא נאמנת, אלא העמד ממון על חזקתו. ולא אזלינן בתר חזקה דגופא לומר: הואיל וספק בידינו על שעת אירוסין מה היא, העמד הגוף על חזקתו של קודם לכן, והרי נולדה בתולה. והכא נמי לא אמרינן העמד הגוף על חזקתו, ובלא מומין נולדה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:2:2.english: Whose [opinion] is it? It is Rabbi Yehoshua, who said - in the first chapter [of Ketubot, regarding a case where] she says, "After you betrothed me I was raped," and he says, "Before I betrothed you" — "we do not live from her mouth" that she should be believed, rather leave the money in its presumptive status. And we do not follow the presumptive status of the body to say: since we are in doubt about the time of betrothal as to what [status] she was [in], leave the body in its previous presumptive status, and behold she was born a virgin. And here too, we do not say: leave the body in its presumptive status, [for] she was born without blemishes.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:3:1.hebrew: אתאן לרבן גמליאל דאמר - דהתם היא נאמנת, דחזקה דגופא עדיפא:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:3:1.english: We arrive at Rabban Gamliel, who said - For there she is deemed credible, since the presumptive status of [her] body is stronger.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:3:2.english: It is broken [i.e., contradictory] - The first clause [of the Mishnah] contradicts the latter clause.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:3:3.hebrew: מי ששנה זו לא שנה זו - רישא לרבי יהושע, והוא הדין לנכנסה לרשות הבעל. וסיפא לרבן גמליאל, וה"ה לעודה בבית אביה, שאין לנו טעם לחלק בין עודה בבית אביה לנכנסה לחופה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:3:3.english: He who taught this did not teach that - The first clause [follows] Rabbi Yehoshua, and the same applies where she entered the husband's domain. And the latter clause [follows] Rabban Gamliel, and the same applies where she is still in her father's house, for we have no reason to distinguish between [when] she is still in her father's house and [when] she entered the bridal canopy.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:4:1.hebrew: לא תימא רבי יהושע לא אזיל בתר חזקה דגופא כלל - אפי' במקום שאין חזקת ממון עומדת נגדה להכחישה:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:4:1.english: Do not say [that] Rabbi Yehoshua does not follow the presumptive status of the body at all - Even in a place where there is no presumptive monetary status standing against it to contradict it.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:4:2.english: Where there is a presumption of monetary [possession] - [that] stands against it, as [in the case] here.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:5:1.english: Impure - For thus the verse writes (Leviticus 13:25): "white hair in the bright white spot."

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:5:2.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: Dull - As Rabba explains.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:5:3.hebrew: כהה טהור - הרי הוא כ״כהה הנגע ממראהו״ שהוא טהור. ומשם ר' משה הדרשן שמעתי: ״ורבי יהושע קיהה, מאי קיהה? אמר רבה: קיהה וטיהר״, כלומר: קיהה בדבר ונחלק עליהם וטיהר [כאדם שנקהו שיניו על אדם שאין משגיח לדבריו]. וכן מצאתי בת"כ: ״ור' יהושע קיהה, טיהר״. אלמא, העמד הגוף על חזקתו ולא תטמאנו מספק:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:5:3.english: Dull — [it is] pure - It is like "the plague has dimmed in its appearance," which is pure. And in the name of Rabbi Moshe HaDarshan I heard [the reading]: "And Rabbi Yehoshua *kihah* [challenged]. What is *kihah*? Rabba said: *Kihah* and declared [it] pure" — that is to say, he took a sharp stance in the matter, disagreed with them, and declared [it] pure [like a person whose teeth are set on edge at someone who pays no heed to his words]. And so I found in Torat Kohanim: "And Rabbi Yehoshua *kihah*, he declared [it] pure." Thus, maintain the body in its presumptive status and do not declare it impure out of doubt.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:6:1.hebrew: רבא אמר רישא כאן נמצאו כאן היו - רבא מהדר לאוקמא כולה כרבן גמליאל, דאוקמינן הלכתא כוותיה בפרק קמא: לעולם חזקה דגופא עדיף. ורישא, טעמא משום דכיון דבבית אביה נמצאו המומין, איתרע חזקתיה דאב, דאיכא למימר: כאן היו קודם אירוסין. ובפ"ק נמי פלוגתייהו בנכנסה לרשות הבעל היא, ובה אמר רבן גמליאל דלא הורעה חזקת אביה בכך:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:6:1.english: Rava said: [In] the first clause, here they were found [and] here they were [created] - Rava seeks to establish the entire [Mishnah] in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, whom we established the law follows in the first chapter: a physical presumption is always stronger. And [in] the first clause, the reason is because since the blemishes were found in her father's house, the father's presumption is weakened, as one can say: they were here prior to betrothal. And in the first chapter as well, their dispute concerns [a case where] she entered the husband's domain, and regarding that [case] Rabban Gamliel said that her father's presumption was not weakened by this.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:7:1.hebrew: משנתארסה לא - אם הביא הבעל ראיה שראו בה מומין הללו משנתארסה והיא עודה בבית אביה, לאו ראיה היא. ואי טעמא משום כאן נמצאו כאן היו, הרי בבית אביה נמצאו. אלא על כרחך רישא וסיפא פליגי, ואפילו באו לדין בעודה בבית אביה, אית ליה לתנא דסיפא דהיא נאמנת:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:7:1.english: From when she was betrothed, no - If the husband brought proof that these blemishes were seen on her after she was betrothed, while she was still in her father's house, it is not [valid] proof. And if the reason is because of "here they were found, here they were [originally]," behold, they were found in her father's house. Rather, perforce, the first clause and the latter clause disagree, and even if they came to court while she was still in her father's house, the Tanna of the latter clause holds that she is believed.

Rashi on Ketubot 75b:8:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - לעולם רישא משום "כאן נמצאו, כאן היו" הוא, ומשנתארסה משום דאיכא תרתי. והיכא שהביא עדים שראו בה מומין הללו משנתארסה בבית אביה, משום הכי לאו ראיה היא, דאיכא תרתי ליפות כחה: חדא — העמד הגוף על חזקתו, ולא היו בה בשעת אירוסין, שהכל הולך אחר אותה שעה; וא"ת: הורעה החזקה הואיל ו"כאן נמצאו", חזקה אין אדם שותה בכוס אא"כ בודקו, ואפי' "כאן היו" קודם קדושין, זה שהכניסה לחופה — וזו היא שתיית הכוס — בידוע שבדקה ונודע לו, וראה וניפייס:
Rashi on Ketubot 75b:8:1.english: He said to him - Actually, the first clause [of the Mishnah] is because of [the principle] "here they were found, here they were," and [the case of] "from after she was betrothed" is because there are two [reasons]. And where he brought witnesses who saw these blemishes on her after she was betrothed, in her father's house, therefore it is not a proof, for there are two [reasons] to strengthen her claim: First, place the body on its presumptive status, [that] they were not on her at the time of betrothal, for everything follows that time; and if you say that the presumption is weakened since "here they were found," [there is] a presumption [that] a person does not drink from a cup unless he examines it, and even [if] "here they were" before the betrothal, this [man] who brought her into the wedding canopy — and this is the drinking of the cup — it is known that he examined her and it became known to him, and he saw and was appeased.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:1:1.hebrew: אבל במומין שבגלוי אין יכול לטעון - תימה: לרב, דמוקי כולה מתני' "כנסה ונמצאו עליה נדרים" בקידשה על תנאי — מה שייך לחלק בין מומין שבסתר למומין שבגלוי, הואיל והתנה על מנת שאין בה מומין? ונראה לרשב"א, דכשהתנה — לא על מומין שבגלוי נתכוין, דאותן ראה ונתפייס, אלא על מומין שלא ראה נתכוין; וכשיש נמי מרחץ באותה העיר, אית לן למימר שלא התנה אלא על מומין שאין נבדקין על ידי מרחץ, כגון ריח הפה ונכפה הקבוע לו זמן. וקאי בין ארשות האב בין ארשות הבעל, וה"ק: אינו יכול לטעון — אפי' הביא הבעל ראיה, אינו מועיל לו כלום:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:1:1.english: "But with regard to visible blemishes, he cannot claim" - It is puzzling: according to Rav, who establishes the entire Mishnah [of] "if he married her and vows were found upon her" as [referring to a case where] he betrothed her on condition, what relevance is there to distinguish between hidden blemishes and visible blemishes, since he stipulated on condition that she have no blemishes? And it appears to Rashba that when he stipulated, he did not intend [to include] visible blemishes, for those he saw and accepted; rather, he intended [to refer only] to blemishes that he did not see. And likewise, when there is a bathhouse in that city, we must say that he only stipulated regarding blemishes that are not detectable through a bathhouse, such as bad breath or epilepsy that has a fixed time. And [this rule] applies both to the father's domain and to the husband's domain; and this is what it means [by] "he cannot claim": even if the husband brings proof [that the blemishes existed beforehand], it does not avail him at all.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:3:1.english: Tavra - Rabbeinu Chananel explained [it to mean] an oath.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:3:2.hebrew: מי ששנה זו לא שנה זו - קשה, דא"כ אמאי נקט ברישא "עודה ברשות האב" וסיפא "נכנסה לרשות הבעל"? איפכא הוה ליה למיתני, דהוה רישא רבותא טפי וסיפא רבותא טפי! ואומר רשב"א דדוקא נקט הכי, דכי היכי דפליגי רישא וסיפא בפלוגתא דר"ג ורבי יהושע, ה"נ פליגי בהכי: דתנא דרישא סבר דדוקא עודה בבית אביה צריך להביא ראיה, אבל נכנסה לרשות הבעל אין צריך להביא ראיה, דאפילו יביא הבעל עדים דעד שלא נתארסה היו בה מומין הללו, כיון שנשאה — חזקה אין אדם שותה בכוס אא"כ בודקו, והאי ראה וניפייס הוא. ותנא דסיפא סבר: אע"ג דנכנסה לרשות הבעל ואיכא למימר "חזקה אין אדם שותה בכוס כו'", כשהביא הבעל ראיה — הוי מקחו מקח טעות, דאין אדם מתפייס במומין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:3:2.english: "He who taught this did not teach that" - This is difficult, for if so, why did [the Mishnah] state in the first clause "while she is still in the father's domain" and [in] the latter clause "if she entered the husband's domain"? It should have taught the opposite, for then the first clause would be a greater novelty and the latter clause would be a greater novelty! And Rashba says that [the Mishnah] specifically stated it thus, for just as the first clause and the latter clause disagree in the dispute of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua, so too do they disagree about this: for the Tanna of the first clause holds that specifically while she is in her father's house [the father] must bring proof, but once she has entered the husband's domain he does not need to bring proof — for even if the husband brings witnesses that these blemishes were on her before she was betrothed, since he married her, there is a presumption that a person does not drink from a cup unless he inspects it, so this [husband] saw [the blemishes] and was reconciled [to them]. And the Tanna of the latter clause holds: even though she entered the husband's domain and one could say "there is a presumption that a person does not drink from a cup, etc.", when the husband brings proof, his acquisition is a mistaken transaction, because a person does not become reconciled to blemishes.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:1.hebrew: אבל היכא דליכא חזקה דממונא אזיל בתר חזקה דגופא - פירוש: אע"ג דאיכא חזקה אחרת כנגד חזקת הגוף — כי הכא, דבלאו חזקת ממון יש חזקה אחרת, ד"העמידנה בחזקת פנויה" — דדוקא כי איכא חזקת ממון לא אלימא ליה חזקת הגוף כנגד חזקת ממון, אבל היכא דליכא חזקת ממון, אלימא ליה חזקת הגוף משאר חזקות. דאי ליכא שום חזקה אחרת כנגדה, מאי אתא לאשמועינן? פשיטא דאזיל בתר חזקת הגוף, כיון דאין דבר מכחישה! וההיא נמי דמייתי, איכא חזקה אחרת כנגדה, כמו שאפרש. ומיהו תימה לר"י: דהיכי מצי למימר דאי לאו חזקת ממון דהכא, הוה אזיל ר' יהושע בתר חזקת הגוף? והא הוי חדא במקום תרתי! דאית לן למימר: "העמידנה בחזקת פנויה". וכי תימא: אדרבה, "העמד אותה בחזקת שלימה, והשתא הוא דנעשה מום" — הרי מום לפניך! דכי האי גוונא חשבינן תרתי לריעותא גבי מקוה שנמדד ונמצא חסר, דאמרי' כל טהרות שנעשו על גביו למפרע, בין ברשות היחיד בין ברשות הרבים, טמאות, משום דאיכא למימר: "העמד טמא על חזקתו ואימור לא טבל", וכי תימא: "העמד מקוה על חזקתו ואימור לא חסר" — הרי חסר לפניך! ונראה לרשב"א דחזקת פנויה לא חשיבא כלל חזקה לגבי חזקת הגוף:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:1.english: "But where there is no presumptive status of money, he follows the presumptive status of the body" - Explanation: Even though there is another presumptive status opposing the presumptive status of the body — as here, where even without the presumptive status of money there is another presumptive status, namely, "Maintain her in the presumptive status of an unmarried woman" — [Rava is saying] that specifically when there is a presumptive status of money, the presumptive status of the body is not strong [enough] for him against the presumptive status of money; however, where there is no presumptive status of money, the presumptive status of the body is stronger for him than other presumptive statuses. For if there were no other presumptive status opposing it, what would [Rava] be coming to teach us? It is obvious that he follows the presumptive status of the body, since there is nothing contradicting it! And that [baraita] as well which [the Gemara] cites — there is another presumptive status opposing it, as I will explain. However, this is difficult for the Ri [R. Yitzchak]: How can [the Gemara] say that were it not for the presumptive status of money here, Rabbi Yehoshua would follow the presumptive status of the body? Why, this is one [presumptive status] in place of two! For we ought to say: "Maintain her in the presumptive status of an unmarried woman." And if you will say: On the contrary, "Maintain her in her presumptive status of being unblemished, and [say that] it is now that the blemish developed" — behold, the blemish is right before you! For in such a case we consider it two [factors] to the detriment [of the status] regarding a mikveh that was measured and found deficient, where we say [that] all ritually pure items that were prepared on its basis retroactively, whether in a private domain or in a public domain, are ritually impure, because one can say: "Maintain the ritually impure person in his presumptive status and say he did not immerse [validly]," and if you will say: "Maintain the mikveh in its presumptive status and say it did not become deficient" — behold, it is deficient right before you! And it appears to the Rashba [R. Shimshon of Sens] that the presumptive status of an unmarried woman is not considered a presumptive status at all relative to the presumptive status of the body.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:2.hebrew: ספק טמא - הקשה רבינו תם: מ"ט דרבנן דאמרי טמא? אמאי לא אזלינן בתר חזקה, דהא אמרינן בפ"ק דחולין (דף י:): "מנא הא מילתא דאמור רבנן אוקי מילתא בתר חזקה", ומייתי לה מקרא! אומר ר"ת: דהכא מיירי כשנזקק לטומאה, שהיה בו נגע אחד — שחין או מכוה — קודם, והיה מוחלט ממנו, וקודם שנטהר נולד בו ספק, ואחר שנטהר מן הראשון לא נשאר בו אלא ספק זה. וכן משמע בשלהי נזיר (דף סה: ושם), דבנזקק לטומאה איירי. והשתא מייתי שפיר דאזיל ר' יהושע בתר חזקה דגופא, דהעמידנו בחזקת שלא היה בו נגע, אע"ג דאיכא חזקה דהעמידנו בחזקת טומאה כנגדה; וה"נ הוה אמרי' לעיל, אי לאו חזקה דממונא. וא"ת: והיכי יליף מהתם? דשאני התם דכתיב קרא, כדיליף בסוף נזיר מ"לטהרו או לטמאו", דפתח בו הכתוב לטהרה תחילה! וי"ל: דמהתם גמרינן. והא דלא אזיל רבי יהושע בתר חזקה דגופא בראוה מדברת ומעוברת בפרק קמא (לעיל כתובות יג.) — משום דמעלה עשו ביוחסין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:2.english: [If it is] uncertain, [he is] impure - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: What is the reason of the Rabbis who say [he is] impure? Why do we not follow the presumptive status [of the body], for we say in the first chapter of Chullin (10b): "From where [is] this matter that the Rabbis said, 'Establish a matter upon its presumptive status'?" — and [the Gemara] derives it from a verse! Rabbeinu Tam says: Here we are dealing with a case where he was already subject to impurity, in that he had one affliction — a boil or a burn — beforehand, and he was confirmed impure from it; and before he became pure, this uncertainty arose in him, and after he became pure from the first [affliction], nothing remained in him except this uncertain [affliction]. And so it is implied at the end of Nazir (65b and there), that it is dealing with one who was already subject to impurity. And now [the Gemara] properly adduces [proof] that Rabbi Yehoshua follows the presumptive status of the body — namely, "leave him in the presumptive status that he did not have an affliction," even though there is a [countervailing] presumptive status of "leave him in the presumptive status of impurity" against it; and similarly we would have said above, were it not for the presumptive status of monetary possession. And if you ask: How does [the Gemara] learn from there? For there it is different, since a verse is written, as [the Gemara] derives at the end of Nazir from "to declare him pure or to declare him impure," because Scripture opened with purity first! And one can answer: We learn from there [as a general principle]. And [as for] why Rabbi Yehoshua does not follow the presumptive status of the body in [the case where] they saw her speaking [with a man] or pregnant in the first chapter (above, Ketubot 13a), [that is] because they set a higher standard with regard to lineage.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:3.hebrew: שער לבן קודם לבהרת טהור - דריש מדכתיב "שער לבן בבהרת", משמע שהבהרת קדמה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:3.english: "[If] the white hair preceded the bright white spot, [he is] pure" - [The Tanna] derives [this] from what is written, "white hair in the bright white spot" — [which] implies that the bright white spot preceded [the white hair].

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:4.hebrew: אמר רבה קיהה וטיהר - רבינו תם גריס רבא, מההיא דהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ פו.) בעובדא דרבה בר נחמני:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:5:4.english: Rabbah said: It became dull, and he declared [him] pure - Rabbeinu Tam reads "Rava," from that [passage] in [the chapter entitled] HaSokher Et HaPo'alim (Bava Metzia 86a), in the incident of Rabbah bar Nachmani.

Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:6:1.hebrew: רישא כאן נמצאו כאן היו - ולא מצי למימר השתא: "העמד רשות האב על חזקתו", דהא איתרע ליה שנמצאו ברשותו; הילכך אזלינן בתר חזקת ממון. והיא אומרת "משארסתני נאנסתי" — התם נמצאת ריעותא ברשות הבעל, שנשאה ולא מצא לה בתולים, ולכך נאמנת לרבן גמליאל, דלא איתרע חזקת רשות האב. ואיירי בענין שיכול להיות שנאנסה תחת בעלה, דאי בענין שודאי לא נאנסה משנשאת — אף על גב שנכנסה לרשות הבעל, איתרע לה חזקת רשות האב, הואיל דודאי ברשות אביה נאנסה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 75b:6:1.english: In the first clause: Here they were discovered, [and] here they were [created] - And one cannot say now, "Maintain the father's domain on its presumptive status," because it has been weakened since they were discovered in his domain; therefore, we follow the presumptive ownership of the money. And [regarding the case where] she says, "After you betrothed me, I was raped" — there, the defect was discovered in the husband's domain, for he married her and did not find her to have tokens of virginity, and therefore she is believed according to Rabban Gamliel, because the presumptive status of the father's domain was not weakened. And [that case] is speaking of a situation where it is possible that she was raped while under her husband['s authority], for if [it were] a situation where she certainly was not raped after she was married — even though she entered the husband's domain, the presumptive status of the father's domain would be weakened, since she was certainly raped in her father's domain.
